shailputri.name: Shailputri
shailputri.intro: Explore schemes and support programmes by age group. These suggestions can help you find possible support, but they do not guarantee eligibility or approval. Other conditions, such as pregnancy, income, or place of residence, may also apply.

lekladki.name: Lek Ladki Yojana
lekladki.description: Financial support is provided in stages from a girl’s birth until she turns 18.
details: Who can apply
Families with one or two girls born on or after 1 April 2023
Families with a yellow or orange ration card
Families with an annual income of up to ₹1 lakh
Maharashtra residents with a bank account in the state
notes: Please confirm the scheme’s current availability and requirements with the department.

sukanya.name: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana
sukanya.description: A savings account for a girl child.
details: Who can open an account
The account can be opened any time from the girl’s birth until she turns 10.
One account can be opened for each girl, with a maximum of two accounts per family.
notes: The interest rate may change every quarter. Please check the current rate with your bank.

icds.name: Anganwadi Services (ICDS)
icds.description: Anganwadi centres offer six services: supplementary nutrition, preschool education, nutrition and health education, vaccination, health check-ups, and referrals. Vaccinations, check-ups, and referrals are provided through the health department, including ASHA and ANM workers.
details: Who can receive these services?
Pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers
Children under 6 years old
Supplementary nutrition is available only to people registered at an Anganwadi centre.

pmmvy.name: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY 2.0)
pmmvy.description: Maternity support for pregnant and breastfeeding women.
details: Who may be eligible
Applicants must meet at least one of these conditions:
Family income below ₹8 lakh
BPL or NFSA ration card
Belong to a Scheduled Caste (SC) or Scheduled Tribe (ST)
Have a disability of 40% or more
Be registered with e-Shram or MGNREGA
Be a woman farmer under PM-KISAN
Be covered under PM-JAY
Applicants must be between 18 years and 7 months and 55 years old. Register within 270 days of the child’s birth.
notes: The scheme was approved under Mission Shakti through FY 2025–26. Its continuation after that period needs confirmation.
Please confirm the scheme’s current availability and requirements with the department.

jssk.name: Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK)
jssk.description: Free care at government health facilities for pregnant women, mothers for up to 42 days after delivery, and sick babies under 1 year old.
details: Who can receive care?
All pregnant women and mothers up to 42 days after delivery at government health facilities
Sick babies under 1 year old can receive free treatment, medicines, tests, and transport.
There are no restrictions based on income, caste, or number of children.

brahmacharini.name: Brahmacharini
brahmacharini.intro: Explore schemes and support programmes by age group. These suggestions can help you find possible support, but they do not guarantee eligibility or approval. Other conditions, such as income, place of residence, or pregnancy, may also apply.

details: Who can open an account?

One account can be opened for each girl, with a maximum of two accounts per family.
notes: The interest rate may change every quarter. Please check the current rate with your bank.

pmposhan.name: PM POSHAN (Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman)
pmposhan.description: Provides one hot, cooked meal each school day to children in government and government-aided schools.
details: Who can receive a meal?
Children in Classes 1 to 8 at government or government-aided schools
Children in Balvatika or pre-primary classes at eligible primary schools
notes: The approved period ended on 31 March 2026. The scheme was extended until 30 September 2026 or until new approval is granted, whichever comes first. Ask the school for the latest information.
Please confirm the scheme’s current availability and requirements with the department.

freeedu.name: Free Professional Education for Girls (Fee Reimbursement)
freeedu.description: Tuition and exam fees are fully reimbursed for eligible professional courses.
details: Who may be eligible?
Girls from EWS, SEBC, or OBC categories, and orphan girls
Families with an annual income of up to ₹8 lakh
Girls admitted to eligible institutions through CAP

pmkvy.name: PMKVY 4.0
pmkvy.description: Short courses and certificates to help people build on their existing skills.
details: Who can participate?
People aged 15 to 59
notes: The scheme was approved through FY 2025–26. The next phase has not yet been confirmed.
Please check with the department to confirm whether the scheme is currently available and what rules apply.

chandraghanta.name: Chandraghanta
chandraghanta.intro: Explore schemes and support programmes by age group. These suggestions can help you find possible support, but they do not guarantee eligibility or approval. Other conditions, such as pregnancy, income, or place of residence, may also apply.

child-marriage.name: Child Marriage-Free Maharashtra
child-marriage.description: It is illegal to marry a girl under 18. People who arrange, conduct, or broker a child marriage may also face legal action.
details: Who can report it?
Anyone can report a child marriage. Their identity will be kept confidential.
notes: Current availability and rules need confirmation with the department.

adishakti.registry: Programme / policy guidance · Registry checked: 10 September 2026
adishakti.name: Adishakti Abhiyan
adishakti.description: A rural campaign that supports women and families by working to reduce malnutrition, maternal and infant deaths, child marriage, and gender-based violence. It also encourages more women to take part in local government.
details: Who it is for
Women and families in rural villages
notes: Current availability and rules need confirmation with the department.

ladki-bahin.description: Provides monthly financial support to women.
details: Who may be eligible?
Women aged 21 to 65 who live in Maharashtra
Families with an annual income of up to ₹2.5 lakh
Married, widowed, divorced, abandoned, or destitute women, or one unmarried woman per family
Women with an Aadhaar-linked bank account
notes: A government resolution dated 18 September 2025 makes yearly e-KYC mandatory. About 92 lakh names were removed by July 2026 following e-KYC checks and verification.

mavim.name: MAVIM Self-Help Groups
mavim.description: Women’s self-help groups (SHGs) can provide savings, loans, training, livelihood opportunities, and access to markets.
details: Who can join?
Women aged 18 or older

umed.name: UMED (Maharashtra State Rural Livelihoods Mission)
umed.description: Provides funding, loans, and training to rural self-help groups (SHGs), including support through the Lakhpati Didi initiative.
details: Who it is for
Rural women who are SHG members

mudra.name: PM Mudra Yojana
details: Who it is for
People running income-generating micro-enterprises in manufacturing, trade, services, or agriculture-related activities

pmegp.name: PMEGP
pmegp.description: Offers a subsidy on bank loans to help set up new micro-enterprises.
details: Who may be eligible?
People aged 18 or older
Applicants must have passed Class 8 to apply for manufacturing projects costing more than ₹10 lakh or service projects costing more than ₹5 lakh.
The scheme supports new businesses only, with one beneficiary per family.
notes: The scheme was approved through FY 2025–26. Its continuation needs confirmation.
Please check with the department to confirm the scheme’s current availability and requirements.

standup.name: Stand-Up India
standup.description: Loans for first-time businesses started by women and SC/ST entrepreneurs.
details: Who may be eligible?
Women entrepreneurs aged 18 or older
Applicants starting their first business
Women must own at least 51% of a business applying as a firm
Applicants must not have defaulted on a bank loan and must contribute at least 10% of the project cost themselves

vishwakarma.name: PM Vishwakarma
vishwakarma.description: Support for artisans in 18 trades, including tailoring.
details: Who may be eligible?
People aged 18 or older who work in one of the 18 trades
Only one person per family can apply. No one in the family can be a government employee.
notes: The target of 30 lakh registrations was reached in September 2026. Check whether registrations are still open.
Current availability and rules need confirmation with the department.

pmfme.name: PMFME
pmfme.description: Support for micro food-processing businesses and self-help groups (SHGs).
details: Who it is for
SHG members applying through UMED in rural areas, or owners of micro food-processing businesses
notes: The scheme has been temporarily extended until 30 September 2026. Further approval is pending.
Current availability and rules need confirmation with the department.

aai.name: “Aai” Women-Centric Tourism Policy
aai.description: Women-owned tourism businesses may receive an interest refund on their loans.
details: Who it is for
Women from Maharashtra who own and run a tourism business
Eligible businesses may include homestays, agri-tourism businesses, restaurants, tour operators, and guide services.

ahilya.name: Punyashlok Ahilyadevi Holkar Mahila Startup Yojana
details: Who it is for
Startups recognised by DPIIT and registered in Maharashtra
At least 51% women-owned and operating for more than one year
Annual revenue between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore
notes: Current availability and rules need confirmation with the department.

eshram.name: e-Shram Registration
eshram.description: Provides an ID (UAN) to unorganised workers to help connect them with schemes.
details: Who it is for
Unorganised workers aged 16 to 59 who are not covered by EPFO or ESIC
